title: Exposed .git repository
why: The .git directory is web-reachable — dump it to recover full source code, secrets and history.
next_step: git-dumper {base}/.git/ loot_git && cd loot_git && git log -p | grep -iE 'pass|secret|key|token'

title: Exposed .git/config
why: Confirms a downloadable git repo and often leaks the remote origin URL (with embedded creds).

title: Exposed .svn metadata
why: Subversion metadata is reachable — reconstruct source and find secrets.

title: Exposed .env file
why: Framework .env files hold DB credentials, API keys and app secrets in cleartext — often instant lateral movement.

title: Exposed AWS credentials file
why: Cleartext AWS keys — pivot straight into the target's cloud account.

title: Exposed SSH private key
why: A downloadable private key is often reusable for SSH into this or a related host.
next_step: curl -s {base}/.ssh/id_rsa -o id_rsa && chmod 600 id_rsa && ssh -i id_rsa user@{host}

title: Exposed .DS_Store (directory listing leak)
why: macOS .DS_Store reveals hidden filenames in the directory to guide further discovery.

title: Exposed .htpasswd
why: HTTP basic-auth password hashes — crack offline with john/hashcat.

title: Apache mod_status exposed
why: Live request table leaks internal URLs, client IPs, and session tokens in query strings.

title: phpinfo() exposed
why: Leaks full server config, paths, loaded modules and environment — great recon for chaining LFI/RCE.

title: phpinfo() exposed (info.php)
why: Same as phpinfo.php — full PHP/server configuration disclosure.

title: Spring Boot Actuator exposed
why: Open actuator endpoints leak env vars, mappings and heap dumps; /env + /refresh or gateway routes can lead to RCE.

title: Spring Boot Actuator /env exposed
why: Dumps environment including DB passwords and cloud credentials; also enables property-injection RCE chains.

title: Spring Boot heapdump downloadable
why: A heap dump contains live secrets, session tokens and passwords — grep the binary for credentials.

title: Tomcat Manager reachable
why: Tomcat Manager with default creds (tomcat/tomcat, admin/admin) lets you deploy a WAR webshell = RCE.
next_step: hydra -C tomcat-defaults.txt {host} http-get /manager/html ; msfconsole -q -x 'use exploit/multi/http/tomcat_mgr_upload;set RHOSTS {host}'

title: Swagger UI exposed
why: Full API documentation — enumerate every endpoint and parameter to test for authz/IDOR/injection.

title: OpenAPI/Swagger spec exposed
why: Machine-readable API map — feed it to your fuzzer/authz tests.

title: GraphQL endpoint (test introspection)
why: If introspection is on you get the entire schema; also test batching/aliasing abuse and IDOR.

title: Elasticsearch REST exposed
why: Unauthenticated Elasticsearch — read/dump every index (often full application data).

title: CouchDB REST exposed
why: Open CouchDB lists databases; older versions allow admin-party account creation -> RCE.

title: web.config downloadable
why: IIS web.config leaks connection strings and machine keys (machineKey enables ViewState RCE).

title: WordPress login found
why: WordPress present — enumerate users/plugins and check for vulnerable plugin versions.

title: robots.txt (path disclosure)
why: Disallowed paths often point straight at admin panels and sensitive directories.

title: Backup archive exposed
why: A downloadable backup usually contains full source and config with secrets.

title: SQL dump exposed
why: A database dump on the webroot leaks users and password hashes directly.

title: security.txt present
why: Not a vuln — notes the security contact and disclosure policy for responsible reporting.
